references.text: Describes how God led his people to his holy place, to the mountain that his right hand has won - the same theme of God's holy mountain and inheritance.
Describes the Lord's foundation on the holy mountains and his love for the gates of Zion - parallel to the sanctuary which the Lord's hands have established.
God's promise to plant Israel in a place where they will dwell securely - a direct parallel to 'you shall bring them in and plant them'.
The image of God planting a vine (Israel) and letting it take root - the same planting motif as in the Exodus text.
Isaiah's parable of the vineyard that God planted on a fruitful mountain - parallel to the planting on the mountain of inheritance.
Zion's mountain as God's holy dwelling - corresponds with 'the mountain which is your inheritance' and 'the place you have made for your dwelling'.
Solomon refers to the temple as a place for God's eternal dwelling - fulfillment of the promise of the sanctuary established by the Lord's hands.
The prophecy that the Lord's house shall stand firm on the mountain - parallel to God's sanctuary established by his hands.
Describes the city with solid foundations, which God has planned and built - New Testament fulfillment of the sanctuary established by the Lord's hands.
The new Jerusalem coming down from heaven, God's dwelling among people - the final fulfillment of God's sanctuary.
Deuteronomy 26:1 expands on the prophetic plan in Exodus 15:17 about bringing the people into their inheritance.
Hebrews uses creation language from Psalm 102 (which reflects Exodus) to show that the sanctuary is part of God's eternal creation.
Psalm 74:2 is a direct theological summary and resumption of the theme in Exodus 15:17 regarding Zion as God's inheritance.
2 Samuel 7:24 confirms the eternal dimension of the 'establishment' of the people that began with their planting in Exodus 15:17.
Psalm 102:26 provides the cosmic background for the language in Exodus 15:17; temple foundation is seen as a new act of creation.
